entries.gloss_en: to draw near, come close, touch (something)
entries.notes: Form I. In Saadia's purity laws (Num 19) consistently means 'touch/come near to' a corpse. Root دنا / دنو.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. دنا: 'دَنا من الشيء دنُوّاً ... قَرُبَ' (drew near); also lane s.v. dnw confirms 'he was, or became, near'

entries.notes: Imperative of مضى Form I. Contexts: Num 22:20 'arise, go with them'; Num 22:35 'go with the people'; Gen 12:1 'go from your land'. The form אמץ' = iMDi (imperative). Apostrophe marks ض (ḍad).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. مضى: 'maDaY He ... passed; went; or went away' and 'imperative xu*o' pattern

entries.notes: Arabicized loan from Persian argawān (red-flowered tree). Lane r0.xml: 'ArjwAn … intensely red; red garments'. Used in Saadia's Tafsir to render Hebrew אַרְגָּמָן (purple/crimson).
entries._grounding: lane r0.xml s.v. أرجوان: 'intensely red; red garments or clothes'

entries.notes: Lane: 'baraSN ... a whiteness which appears upon the exterior of the body'. Used throughout Lev 13 for the skin-disease rendering Hebrew צָרַעַת. The ץ = ص (ṣad).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. برص: 'baraSN ... a certain disease ... a whiteness incident in the skin'

entries.notes: Imperative of أخذ Form I; Lane: 'imperative xu*o'. The כ' marks خ (khā'); ד marks ذ (dhāl). Surface וכד also represents the same imperative with wāw prefix.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أخذ: 'A^xa*a ... imperative xu*o, originally A@w^oxu*o'

entries.notes: 2mp imperfect of أكل. Lane: 'A^akalahu ... He ate it'. The inflected form covers negated contexts (Gen 3:3 'do not eat thereof') and affirmative (Gen 45:18 'you shall eat').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أكل: 'A^akalahu ... He ate it, namely, food'

entries.notes: Lisan: 'السَّجْفُ والسِّجْفُ: السِّتْر'. Used by Saadia to render the Tabernacle parokhet/veil in Ex 26:33, Num 4:5, Num 18:7.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. سجف: 'السَّجْفُ والسِّجْفُ: السِّتْر' (the curtain/veil)

entries.gloss_en: Kadesh; Saadia's Arabic name for Kadesh-Barnea
entries.notes: Saadia consistently uses רקים to render the biblical place-name קָדֵשׁ (Kadesh/Kadesh-Barnea); Num 20:1, 20:14, 13:26. The Arabic رقيم (raqīm) means 'inscribed/written' and was a known geographic name. Not a Lane entry for this toponym.
entries._grounding: Blau does not attest this toponym; Lane has رقم s.v. 'He wrote', but the proper-noun use is Saadia's rendering of קדש

entries.gloss_en: a sojourner who has entered the community; resident alien
entries.notes: Blau: 'neophyte, convert, proselyte / הנכנס לדת'. In Saadia's Num 15 contexts, אלג'ריב אלדכ'יל renders 'the sojourner who sojourns among you'. The apostrophe marks خ (khā').
entries._grounding: blau s.v. دخيل: 'neophyte, convert, proselyte / הנכנס לדת'

entries.notes: Preposition بـ with 2mp pronominal suffix كم. Lane attests بِكُم as standard compound. Num 14:28 'as you have spoken before Me'; Num 33:56 'as I planned to do to them, so I will do to you'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. بـ (preposition): بِكُمْ = 'with/to you (plural)' — standard pronominal compound

entries.gloss_en: he lived, passed his life (a number of years)
entries.notes: 3ms perfect of عاش (Form I of عيش). Lane: 'EaA$a He lived'. Contexts: Gen 11:11–13 'and he lived after that N years'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عيش: 'EaA$a ... He lived; he passed life in a particular manner'

entries.notes: Form II imperative of قرب (qarraba = to bring near, offer). Lane qrb s.v. 2: 'He brought [it] near'. Blau also attests Form II 'to be sacrificed (offerings)'. Used throughout Num 28 for making burnt offerings.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قرب Form II: 'He brought near'; blau s.v. قرب Form II: 'to be sacrificed (offerings)'

entries.notes: Biblical proper noun: Aram/Arameans (Heb. אֲרָם). Saadia transcribes ארם directly. Lane has آرام as arabicized form of the name. Appears Gen 10:23, Gen 22:21, Num 23:7.
entries._grounding: proper noun transcription; Lane has no entry for this toponym, but standard Arabic form is آرام

entries.gloss_en: wild animals, beasts of the field
entries.notes: Lisan: 'الوَحْش: كلُّ شيء من جواب البَرّ مما لا يَسْتأْنس' (every creature of the wilderness that is not domesticated). Used Gen 1:25, 1:30, 2:19 to render חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה/חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. وحش: 'كلُّ شيء من جواب البَرّ مما لا يَسْتأْنس' (wild land animals)

entries.gloss_en: he counted, enumerated, took a census of
entries.notes: Form I of عدّ. Lisan: 'العَدُّ: إِحْصاءُ الشيءِ، عَدَّه ... عَدّاً وتَعْداداً' (counting, enumeration). Num 26:63–64: 'those whom Moses and Aaron counted (عدا) among Bnei Yisrael'. Root doubled-د.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. عدد: 'العَدُّ: إِحْصاءُ الشيءِ، عَدَّه يَعُدُّه عَدّاً'

entries.notes: أب 'father' with 1cp suffix -نا (our). Num 27:3–4 'our father died'; Gen 19:31 'our father is old'. Standard Arabic morphology; Lane s.v. أبو.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ابو: أبونا = 'our father', nominal with first-person plural suffix

entries.notes: From بر (open country/land). Asas Zamakhshari confirms 'نزلوا بالبرية' = 'they camped in the wilderness'. Lisan s.v. بر. Used throughout Num to render מִדְבַּר.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. بر (open land) and asas-zamakhshari s.v. برية confirming 'wilderness'

entries.notes: Used in construction ما خلا (mā khalā) = 'except'. Lane khw/khlw: 'xalaA commencing with xalaA as a word denoting exception'. Num 18:3, 28:23, 28:31: 'everything except the vessels of holiness'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. خلو (xalaA): 'xalaA as a word denoting exception'

entries.gloss_en: sound, whole, without defect (animals for sacrifice)
entries.notes: Acc./adv. form of صِحاح (sound, healthy). Lane s.v. صح: 'He was, or became, healthy, or sound; or restored to health'. Used Num 28:3,11,19 to qualify sacrificial lambs: 'without defect'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صح: 'SaH~a ... He was, or became, healthy, or sound'

entries.notes: Plural of تليد / abstract of ولد root. Lane s.v. ولد: 'wilaAdahN ... walaAdN'. In Saadia, consistently renders Hebrew תּוֹלְדוֹת in genealogical headings (Gen 10:1, 11:10, 11:27) and census formulas (Num 1:20,22,24).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ولد: birth, generation, progeny

entries.notes: Form I of دعا. Lisan: 'ادْعوا شُهداءكم ... اسْتَغِيثوا بهم'. Num 21:3 'God hearkened to the prayer/call of Israel'; Gen 12:8 'called out by His name'; Gen 20:8 'summoned all his servants'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. دعا: 'الدُّعاءُ ... اسْتَغاثَ, سَأَل'

entries.notes: Passive participle of لعن. Lisan: 'رجل لَعِينٌ ومَلْعُونٌ'. Gen 3:14 'you are cursed above all beasts'; Gen 27:29; Num 24:9: 'those who curse you shall be cursed'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. لعن: 'رجل لَعِينٌ ومَلْعُونٌ ... اللَّعْنُ: الإِبْعادُ والطَّرْد من الخير'

entries.gloss_en: chest, coffer; the Ark of the Covenant
entries.notes: Lane s.v. صندق: 'SunoduwqN ... A chest, coffer, or trunk'. In Saadia: consistently renders אֲרוֹן הָעֵדוּת (Ark of the Testimony/Covenant). Lisan confirms: 'الصُّنْدوق: الجُوالِق'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صندق: 'SunoduwqN ... A chest, coffer, or trunk'

entries.gloss_en: the priests (Saadia's term for the Kohanim)
entries.notes: Blau: 'إمام ... not only leader but mainly priest / לא רק מנהיג בכלל, אלא בעיקר כהן'. Saadia uses this to render כֹּהֵן (priest) and כֹּהֲנִים throughout the Tafsir.
entries._grounding: blau s.v. إمام: 'not only leader but mainly priest / כהן'

entries.notes: Lane s.v. حرب. Standard classical Arabic: the noun حَرْب (war, battle). Blau also confirms Form I 'to wage war'. Num 10:9 'if you go to war'; Num 24:20 'first in war among nations'; Num 31:14 'returning from battle'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حرب: 'Harabahu ... He despoiled him'; lane lists noun حَرب (war) throughout the entry

entries.gloss_en: and take! (imperative of أخذ with wāw)
entries.notes: ו + imperative خُذْ (from أخذ). Same lemma as כ'ד (id: khud-take-imperative); listed separately because the surface וכד lacks the apostrophe variant. Same root, same meaning.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أخذ: imperative xud

entries.notes: Verbal noun of pattern mafʿal from كسب (to gain/earn). Lane s.v. كسب: 'He collected [wealth]; he gained, acquired, or earned'. Phrase 'כל צנעה' מכסב' = 'every work of gain/earning' in festival laws (Num 28:18, 25, 26) renders מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كسب: 'kasaba ... He gained, acquired, or earned, wealth'

entries.notes: Plural of صَمْغ. Lisan: 'الصَّمْغُ ... شيء يَنْضَحُه الشجر ويَسيل منها' (what exudes and flows from trees = gum). Blau: 'resin / קרף'. Used for בְּשָׂמִים/סַמִּים (spices/incense) Ex 25:6, 30:7, Num 4:16.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. صمغ: 'شيء يَنْضَحُه الشجر' (gum/resin); blau s.v. صمغ: 'resin / קרף'

entries.notes: Form I of قبل. Lane: 'qabila He took, received, or admitted, willingly, or with approbation; he accepted'. Num 16:15 'do not accept their offering'; Num 27:20 'so the community will accept him'; Deut 13:9 'do not listen to him'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قبل: 'qabila He took, received ... with approbation; he accepted'

entries.gloss_en: stranger, foreigner; one who is not native
entries.notes: Adjective used as noun. Lane s.v. غرب: 'garaba ... He became [a stranger, a foreigner; or] far, or distant, from his home'. In Saadia, renders גֵּר (sojourner) in Num 15, Gen 17:12. Apostrophe marks غ (ghayn).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. غرب: 'garaba ... He became a stranger, a foreigner'

entries.gloss_en: to permit, allow, give leave (to do something)
entries.notes: Form IV imperfect passive/active of طلق. Lane s.v. طلق Form IV: 'ATlq lahu fiEola ka*aA He permitted him, or gave him permission or leave, to do such a thing'. Gen 41:34; Gen 43:14; Deut 18:14.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. طلق Form IV: 'ATlq lahu ... He permitted him, or gave him permission or leave'

entries.gloss_en: my soul; myself; my own accord
entries.notes: نفس + 1cs suffix. Lane: 'nafasN ... soul, spirit, self, person'. 'ליס מן תלקא נפסי' (Num 16:28) = 'not of my own accord'. 'ותחיא נפסי' (Gen 12:13) = 'my soul will live'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. نفس: 'nafsN ... The soul; the spirit; self'

entries.notes: fa- (then/so) + 3ms perfect مَدَّ (Form I of مدد). Lisan: 'المَدُّ: الجَذْب والمَطْلُ. مَدَّه يَمُدُّه مَدّاً' (stretching out). Gen 19:10 'the men stretched out their hands'; Gen 22:10; Gen 48:14 'Israel stretched out his right hand'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. مدد: 'المَدُّ: الجَذْب والمَطْلُ. مَدَّه يَمُدُّه مَدّاً'

entries.notes: Form I perfect/imperative of وقف. Lane: 'waqafa He was, or became, still, or stationary; he stood still; he continued standing'. Also used as imperative 'قف' = stand/stop. Num 22:24; Num 23:3, 15.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. وقف: 'waqafa He was, or became, still, or stationary; he stood still'

entries.notes: Biblical proper noun; Saadia renders יְהוֹשֻׁעַ as יהושע (Hebrew letters, unchanged). Num 11:28, 13:16, 14:6. Not a dictionary entry.
entries._grounding: proper noun; no lexicon entry needed

entries.notes: Lane s.v. كبد: 'kabid [or liver]'. Standard classical term. Ex 29:13,22: 'the lobe of the liver' (זאידה' אלכבד). Deut 4:11: 'to the heart/midst of the heaven' (כبد السماء).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كبد: 'kabadahu ... He ... hit, or smote, or hurt, his kabid [or liver]'

entries.notes: منزل + 2ms/2mp suffix. Lane s.v. نزل: manziluN = 'a place of alighting, or abiding; a dwelling-place, house'. Num 18:11,13: 'every clean person in your household may eat it'; Deut 11:19.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. نزل: 'manzilN ... a place of alighting ... a dwelling-place'

entries.notes: Lane s.v. نصف: 'AlnaSofN ... one of the two halves of a thing'. Num 12:12 'half his flesh eaten away'; Num 15:10; Num 28:14 'half a hin for each bull'. The ץ = ص (ṣad).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. نصف: 'النِّصْفُ: أَحد شقَّي الشيء' (one half of something)

entries.notes: Dual of عَتُود (a young he-goat ready for mating). Lane s.v. عتد: 'Eatuda ... It (a thing) was, or became, ready, at hand'. The noun عَتُود / عَتِيد means 'prepared/ready male goat'. Num 7:17,23,29 etc.: 'five he-goats' (five of عتدان in the texts).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عتد: the noun 'Eatwdap' (young male goat) within the entry

entries.notes: Form I of كشف. Lane: 'ka$afahu He uncovered it; unveiled it; laid it open; displayed it; exposed it to view'. Gen 9:21 'exposed himself in his tent'; Ex 20:23 'lest you expose your nakedness'; Lev 18:7.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كشف: 'ka$afahu He uncovered it; unveiled it; laid it open'

needs_manual.reason: Saadia's transliteration of Hebrew בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם ('between the two evenings'); the form does not correspond to any lexicon entry in Lane/Lisan/Blau. Included as proper-noun entry with explanatory note.
